items.contract: The administrator imports an initial definition or exact accepted baseline; the workspace validates it, identifies the state, durably stores it, and opens that state.
rules: RULE-7 requires accepted baseline import to be atomic.
RULE-9 makes packaged kernel verify authoritative.
items.actorBoundary: Real local browser and Spring HTTP application backed by PostgreSQL 18.6 and packaged School Kernel
items.claim: Both explicit import modes and the exact accepted archive complete through the actor boundary and persist the corresponding lifecycle state.

evidence.observation: POST of the real definition returns 200; assertions compare INITIAL_DRAFT, no accepted timetable, school ID, import mode, ETag, version 1, and the complete stored definition tree.
POST of a definition and packaged-plan result returns 200; assertions compare ACCEPTED_BASELINE and both complete stored JSON trees.
The browser journey observed Initial draft and No accepted timetable after importing examples/initial-school.json, with zero console errors or warnings.

counterEvidence: The kernel v1 definition schema has no school-level display-name field, so the fixture is shown by stable school ID with an explicit unavailable-name cue rather than by a definition-supplied school display name.

items.contract: A result alone is rejected with a matching-definition explanation and no import.
rules: RULE-22 requires safe stable failure output.
items.actorBoundary: Real HTTP import route
items.claim: A result-only upload returns MATCHING_DEFINITION_REQUIRED and leaves the exact empty aggregate.

evidence.observation: Assertions require HTTP 422, code MATCHING_DEFINITION_REQUIRED, no assignments text, EMPTY, version 0, and {} JSONB.

items.contract: An accepted archive must contain exactly the three safe root entries; absent, duplicate, extra, unreadable, or unsafe content rejects the import.
rules: RULE-14 defines exact bounded no-extraction ZIP parsing.
items.actorBoundary: Multipart HTTP import and bounded archive reader
items.claim: Exact archives import; extra and traversal entries are rejected without mutation or filesystem extraction.

evidence.observation: The exact archive reaches ACCEPTED_BASELINE; a second archive with ../extra.json returns 422 UNSAFE_ARCHIVE and the row remains exactly empty.
The reader accepts the exact entry set in memory, while the unsafeArchive test rejects traversal content.

items.contract: Parsing, version, identity, revision, assignment, hard-validity, or lineage failure names a safe reason and persists or discloses nothing.
rules: RULE-26 requires the independent direct hard-feasibility verifier.
items.actorBoundary: Packaged verify process followed by real HTTP import
items.claim: Strict kernel verification rejects malformed, unsupported, mismatched, incomplete, tampered, and hard-invalid documents before workspace mutation.

evidence.observation: Successor-only and definition/result revision mismatch return exit 2 and structured INVALID_INPUT with no timetable.
The same BaselineVerifier production path rejects tampering, lineage and school mismatch, duplicates, missing assignments, and hard collisions before solving.
Malformed HTTP input returns 422 and exact EMPTY/version 0/{} state.

items.contract: Definition-only import containing basedOnRevision is rejected without state change.
items.actorBoundary: Packaged School Kernel verify process
items.claim: Successor-only input returns INVALID_INPUT and cannot reach persistence.

evidence.observation: The test adds basedOnRevision to the initial definition and asserts exit 2 and status INVALID_INPUT.

items.contract: A definition/result import requires a complete FEASIBLE result matching the exact definition.
rules: RULE-9 baseline mode requires exact definition revision and direct hard validity.
items.actorBoundary: Packaged verify process and accepted-pair HTTP route
items.claim: Only an exact complete verified pair becomes ACCEPTED_BASELINE.

evidence.observation: A packaged-plan FEASIBLE result verifies with definitionRevision and timetableRevision equal by value.
The verified pair is stored atomically as the complete accepted definition, result, and manifest.

items.contract: Durable-storage failure reports incomplete import, exposes no accepted baseline, and leaves the workspace empty.
items.actorBoundary: Real HTTP and PostgreSQL transaction with injected trigger failure
items.claim: An accepted-pair write failure rolls back the entire state transition.

evidence.observation: A BEFORE UPDATE trigger raises an error; HTTP returns 503, then assertions require EMPTY, version 0, and {} JSONB.

items.contract: Definition-only creates a draft; verified pair creates an accepted baseline; invalid input is never current.
items.actorBoundary: Real HTTP import representations and PostgreSQL state
items.claim: Import modes have distinct durable lifecycle and acceptedTimetable values.

evidence.observation: Definition mode asserts INITIAL_DRAFT and acceptedTimetable false; accepted-pair mode at line 115 asserts ACCEPTED_BASELINE and true.

items.contract: Identifiers are exact and names, weekdays, ordering, and optional times come from metadata rather than ID spelling.
rules: RULE-8 forbids reconstructing kernel documents or interpreting IDs.
items.actorBoundary: Stored JSONB snapshot and native browser presentation
items.claim: The complete imported document is retained by value and the browser never parses IDs into meaning.

evidence.observation: The test compares the complete stored initialDefinition tree to the uploaded bytes parsed as JSON.
Presentation consumes explicit displayName/id fields; missing school name receives an explicit unavailable-name cue.

counterEvidence: The current kernel contract does not provide a school-level display name, so the school ID is visibly used with an unavailable-name cue.

items.contract: Without a manifest, imported locks are persistent policy.
items.actorBoundary: Accepted-pair import manifest generation
items.claim: Every imported period/room lock is recorded with PERSISTENT_POLICY origin.

evidence.observation: A definition with one period lock and one room lock yields sorted manifest entries whose origins are both PERSISTENT_POLICY.

items.contract: Validation is isolated and accepts no unsupported schema or catalog version.
rules: RULE-24 requires disposable PostgreSQL and packaged CLI.
items.actorBoundary: Packaged kernel and isolated PostgreSQL Testcontainers application
items.claim: Every import journey uses isolated state and strict versioned schemas.

evidence.observation: Unsupported versions and coercive scalar types are rejected by the strict schema pipeline.
The HTTP suite starts postgres:18.6 in a disposable container and resets the singleton row before each test.

items.contract: Rejected or interrupted import persists no partial state and makes data unavailable beyond the local machine.
rules: RULE-21 requires loopback, Host/Origin, CSRF, and no CORS.
items.actorBoundary: Real HTTP security and PostgreSQL state
items.claim: Every tested refusal leaves exact empty state and the listener accepts only the configured local origin/port.

evidence.observation: Missing CSRF, hostile Origin, and absent Origin all return 403 and assert the exact empty row.
Hostile Host, wrong loopback port, CORS preflight, traversal, login, and actuator routes are denied without secret disclosure.

items.contract: Success leaves exactly one durable initial draft or verified accepted baseline.
items.actorBoundary: PostgreSQL singleton aggregate after HTTP success
items.claim: Both successful modes leave version 1 and exactly the corresponding complete document state.

evidence.observation: Definition and accepted-pair tests assert lifecycle, version, and complete JSON values after the response.

items.contract: Failure leaves the workspace empty and discloses or accepts no candidate timetable.
items.actorBoundary: Real HTTP failure responses and PostgreSQL row
items.claim: All import refusal families assert the canonical empty row and candidate absence.

evidence.observation: Result-only, malformed, missing If-Match, and stale requests assert EMPTY/version 0/{}; result-only body lacks assignments.

items.contract: UC-1 has no Requires, Includes, or Extends relations.
items.actorBoundary: Feature relationship graph
items.claim: UC-1 is an eligible root and does not consume an unapproved use case.

evidence.observation: The UC-1 relation block lists none for all three relation types.

items.contract: Separate resource-only contract, CLI, and workspace modules preserve the process boundary and the contract JAR has no classes.
items.actorBoundary: Clean Maven reactor and compiled workspace classes
items.claim: The reactor graph and bytecode enforce the required module/process separation.

evidence.observation: ArchUnit finds no workspace production dependency on kernel implementation packages.
jar tf filtered for .class returned no entries after clean verify.

items.contract: The pinned Java/Spring/PostgreSQL stack is used and excluded persistence/frontend stacks and Timefold internals are absent.
items.actorBoundary: Effective Maven reactor and clean Java 25 build
items.claim: The clean reactor uses the selected versions and allowed technology set.

evidence.observation: mvn -q clean verify passed under Java 25; PostgreSQL 18.6 Testcontainers started; dependency tree resolved Jackson 3.2.2 and source checks found no Timefold .impl import.

items.contract: One relationally guarded JSONB singleton is the sole workspace persistence model and uses JdbcClient SQL.
items.actorBoundary: Fresh PostgreSQL schema and repository
items.claim: The exact singleton guard columns and one authoritative JSONB document round-trip without a second store.

evidence.observation: Assertions compare state/version and complete stored JSONB after import; the migration creates only workspace_aggregate and its singleton seed.

items.contract: Flyway is the only schema authority and fresh state contains one EMPTY aggregate with no school data.
items.actorBoundary: Spring startup against fresh PostgreSQL 18.6
items.claim: Flyway validates and applies the sole forward migration to the exact empty singleton.

evidence.observation: Flyway reported an empty schema, validated one migration, applied V1, and the before-each assertions read EMPTY/version 0/{}.

counterEvidence: There is no retained prior migration state yet; checksum-drift startup refusal is configured through Flyway validation but not exercised by a dedicated test in this checkpoint.

items.contract: Exactly eight lifecycle values exist and every unlisted transition is refused without side effects.
items.actorBoundary: Import application service and conditional PostgreSQL mutation
items.claim: UC-1 allows only EMPTY to INITIAL_DRAFT or ACCEPTED_BASELINE; occupied import is refused with exact state preservation.

evidence.observation: After a first import, a second returns 409 INVALID_WORKSPACE_TRANSITION and assertions compare the prior version and entire JSON document unchanged.

negativeObligations: No process launch after occupied-state check
counterEvidence: Transitions belonging exclusively to later use cases are represented in the enum/migration but are not executable routes yet.

items.contract: Strong ETag/If-Match and the same SQL version guard serialize every mutation with exact 428/412 failures and one racing winner.
items.actorBoundary: Real HTTP requests racing against conditional PostgreSQL SQL
items.claim: Missing and stale preconditions do not mutate; simultaneous same-version imports yield exactly one durable winner.

evidence.observation: Two virtual-thread POSTs with the same ETag produce sorted statuses [200,412], state INITIAL_DRAFT, version 1, and one exact definition tree.

items.contract: Accepted-bundle import stores all accepted fields and advances state in one rollback-safe transaction.
items.actorBoundary: Transactional JdbcClient update
items.claim: The accepted pair is one JSONB replacement and an injected database failure leaves every guard/document value unchanged.

evidence.observation: A trigger rejects the one update; the post-failure row is exactly EMPTY/version 0/{} with no accepted baseline.

items.contract: Kernel JSON fidelity and canonical revision semantics are preserved without ID interpretation or display-model reconstruction.
items.actorBoundary: Canonical process files, JSONB storage, and browser snapshot
items.claim: Imported documents round-trip by JSON value and canonical process bytes use the kernel RFC 8785 implementation.

evidence.observation: Accepted definition and result nodes are compared in full to the uploaded document trees.
Independent RFC 8785 vectors and definition/timetable revision scope tests pass.

items.contract: verify is a structured, non-solving public command covering both modes and all named integrity checks.
items.actorBoundary: Packaged school-kernel executable
items.claim: The command returns schema-valid VERIFIED/INVALID_INPUT evidence with correct exit codes and no timetable or solver invocation.

evidence.observation: Six packaged-process tests cover both modes, malformed/successor/mismatch input, no solve controls/logs/candidate, token/byte bounds, schema validity, and concurrent publication.

counterEvidence: Several baseline mutation families are asserted through the same shared BaselineVerifier in packaged replan tests rather than repeated individually through verify.

items.contract: Every kernel invocation uses private bounded temporary files/streams, no debug, explicit correlation, and cleanup.
items.actorBoundary: Workspace KernelVerifier process adapter
items.claim: Verify runs in a new owner-only directory with distinct files, capped drains, safe structured output, and finally cleanup.

evidence.observation: The adapter creates a temp directory, applies POSIX owner permissions, writes distinct canonical inputs/output, passes correlation-id, bounds both drains to 64 KiB retained data, and deletes the tree in finally.

negativeObligations: No accepted/import file used as output
counterEvidence: Private permission, oversized child-output, and cleanup failure families are established by code inspection rather than dedicated adapter fault-injection tests in this checkpoint.

items.contract: Import JSON/manifest/archive sizes and exact ZIP structure are bounded and entries are never extracted.
items.actorBoundary: SafeImportReader before packaged kernel invocation
items.claim: Bounded stream reads reject size, count, duplicate, missing, extra, directory, traversal, separator, encrypted/unreadable, truncation, and bomb forms before persistence.

evidence.observation: Exact archive parsing succeeds in memory; extra/traversal and over-limit document forms are rejected.
Compressed, per-entry, total-uncompressed and entry-count bounds are checked while reading ZipInputStream; only exact root names enter an in-memory map and no extraction API is used.

counterEvidence: The full one-byte boundary and malformed-archive matrix named by the rule is not represented by separate test cases; only representative over-limit and unsafe forms are automated here.

items.contract: The local no-identity surface is loopback-only, same-origin, CSRF-protected, CORS-disabled, and narrowly routed.
items.actorBoundary: Real Tomcat HTTP server and Spring Security chain
items.claim: Only the UC-1 route subset and static workspace are reachable on the configured loopback origin/port.

evidence.observation: The test proves root redirect and workspace asset success, while login/actuator/CORS preflight/hostile Host/wrong local port/traversal are denied; mutation tests cover valid, missing, and hostile CSRF/Origin.

items.contract: Failures use the stable safe JSON problem shape and mapped HTTP statuses without technical or candidate disclosure.
items.actorBoundary: Real HTTP error responses
items.claim: UC-1 failure families return stable codes/status/state/ETag/correlation fields and safe messages.

evidence.observation: The suite asserts 403,409,412,422,428,503 mappings, stable codes, state/correlation where applicable, and absence of assignments/secrets.

counterEvidence: Dedicated production-response scans for every prohibited token are not separate tests; representative candidate, secret, and password disclosures are asserted absent.

items.contract: Logs are safe structured stderr summaries and retain only required non-sensitive validation evidence.
items.actorBoundary: Workspace process adapter logging
items.claim: Normal import logs only correlation ID, verify command, exit class, and elapsed time and never log school documents.

evidence.observation: Each verify completion line contains correlationId, kernelCommand=verify, exitClass, and elapsedTimeMs; no definition/result/display name/assignment/path appears.

counterEvidence: Captured logging tests for every failure class are not present as a dedicated test family in this checkpoint.

items.contract: Each use case has real HTTP and browser success journeys on disposable PostgreSQL 18.6; kernel-dependent paths use the packaged CLI.
items.actorBoundary: Maven verify, PostgreSQL Testcontainers, packaged launcher, and browser
items.claim: UC-1 has all required outer-boundary success and negative journeys with no database substitute.

evidence.observation: 96 tests passed with 0 failures/errors/skips; logs show postgres:18.6, Flyway, ephemeral Tomcat, and packaged verify invocations.
A real browser imported the fixture and observed the durable initial-draft state with no console errors or warnings.

items.contract: Typed handlers, shared loading/baseline verification, independent hard validation, exhaustive mappings, and no Throwable catch preserve kernel boundaries.
items.actorBoundary: Compiled kernel architecture and packaged commands
items.claim: Plan/replan/verify share strict production pipelines and only the CLI constructs adapters/maps sealed outcomes.

evidence.observation: Four architecture tests assert CLI-only adapter construction, separate handlers returning the sealed outcome family, absence of catch(Throwable), and public Timefold boundary; packaged tests exercise the shared paths.

items.contract: One immutable catalog and manifest-derived kernel version drive all metadata; solver uses only public SolverManager/SolverJob APIs.
items.actorBoundary: Kernel metadata tests and compiled architecture
items.claim: Catalog fields are exact, malformed package version fails safely, and no internal Timefold API is referenced.

evidence.observation: The test compares the complete catalog version, ordered IDs, categories, and weights by value.
ArchUnit rejects Timefold types outside the solver adapter package and any .impl dependency; solver integration uses SolverManager/SolverJob.

items.contract: Kernel inputs are byte/token/depth bounded and atomic publication is exactly-one without force and replacement with force.
items.actorBoundary: Unit file boundary and concurrent packaged verify processes
items.claim: Every numeric boundary is tested and concurrent publication preserves complete destination bytes with exit 74 for refusal.

evidence.observation: Depth 64, string 1 MiB, and number 100 are each tested below/at/above; byte tests do the same at 10 MiB.
Two unforced publishers yield [0,74] and schema-valid output; forced publishers both succeed and the last completed correlation ID owns a complete output.

counterEvidence: Controlled crash and injected filesystem capability/close/link/move failures are not all represented as packaged-process fault-injection cases; lower-level atomic boundary tests cover ordinary supported-filesystem behavior.
